corpus.title: Indonesia races to find 129 missing after Java Sea ferry capsizes
corpus.signal_text:
Indonesia races to find 129 missing after Java Sea ferry capsizes

Indonesia intensified its search operation on 14 September for 129 people still missing after the Virgo Transport 8 ferry capsized in rough seas in the Java Sea the previous day. By then, 108 survivors had been rescued and six bodies recovered.

corpus.title: Sjamsudin Noor Air Base serves as Virgo evacuation point
corpus.signal_text:
"Four dead victims were evacuated today from a vessel near the accident site and flown to Sjamsudin Noor Air Base," Air Base Commander Col. Hilman L.P. Ambarita said in Banjarbaru.
The four body bags arrived at the air base in separate helicopter flights.
Basarnas' Dauphin HR 3601 helicopter was the first to land at about 11:25 a.m. local time, carrying two body bags.
About 30 minutes later, a police helicopter arrived at 11:54 a.m., carrying two more body bags.
The four victims had been aboard the tugboat KM TB TCB, which was being used as a support vessel near the Virgo Transport 8 accident site.
Upon arrival at Sjamsudin Noor Air Base, the victims were quickly and systematically transferred from the helicopters.
The four body bags were transferred to ambulances and taken to Bhayangkara Hospital in Banjarmasin.
At the hospital, police DVI teams will examine the bodies and conduct identification procedures to confirm each victim's identity.
Ambarita said air evacuation efforts on the third day of the search-and-rescue operation focused on transporting dead victims from the support vessel to medical facilities ashore.
Each victim arriving at Sjamsudin Noor Air Base immediately received initial medical attention before being handed over to relevant authorities for identification and further handling.
The support was part of Sjamsudin Noor Air Base's role in the search-and-rescue operation for the Virgo Transport 8 accident.
"Besides supporting air operations, Sjamsudin Noor Air Base is an important point for receiving and evacuating victims found in the Java Sea," he said.

corpus.title: Bad weather hampers Indonesia ferry rescue, dozens still missing
corpus.signal_text:
Bad weather hampers Indonesia ferry rescue, dozens still missing
"We cannot fight nature; the swells and waves in the area were extremely high," said the national search and rescue agency, Basarnas.
BANJARMASIN, Indonesia: Indonesian rescuers brought ashore on Tuesday (Sep 15) nearly two dozen survivors from a passenger ship that capsized off Java island at the weekend, their evacuation delayed by bad weather, officials said.
Dozens of people remain unaccounted for three days after the Virgo Transport 8, which carried 213 passengers and 30 crew, went down early Sunday.
Six people have died while a total of 108 have been rescued alive and 129 others are still missing, the national search and rescue agency, Basarnas, said in a statement Tuesday. The death toll and the missing figure have remained unchanged since Sunday.
The ferry had lost contact with its shipping company shortly after departing from Indonesia's second-largest city of Surabaya on Java island, headed for Banjarmasin on Borneo.
Footage released by the rescue agency on Monday showed the capsized vessel with a part of the hull visible above the waterline.
Basarnas said that 22 survivors were brought to a harbour in Banjarmasin on Tuesday, after bad weather had prevented their rescue a day earlier.
"The plan was to evacuate them to Trisakti Port yesterday, but adverse weather conditions prevented us from doing so," local search and rescue agency head I Putu Sudayana told reporters.
"We cannot fight nature; the swells and waves in the area were extremely high."
Four bodies were also airlifted to Banjarmasin Tuesday, Basarnas said.
Nearly 1,100 rescuers, including from the navy and police, were involved in the search operation, which also included more than a dozen vessels and five aircraft, the agency said.
Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.
Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.
